narrative.overview: Factory-Records catalog identity fused to a software studio: matte void-black board, pulse-ink hairline graphics, engraved industrial display caps, mono body text, and a numbering system that treats everything the studio makes as a pressed release. Every section is a numbered entry; every future case study takes the next number. One deliberate divergence from the source world: Factory withheld; we label — the offer and the action stay in plain words within seconds.
keyCharacteristics: Matte Void ground, Pulse hairline ink, Industrial gray secondary — color only as coded blocks
Engraved (outline) Technor display caps over Martian Mono body
Catalog-number grammar on every entry; hairline radial pulse plot as the signature graphic
Contact red is reserved: the contact entry alone owns a hue

rules.name: The Code Rule
rules.body: Color hues appear only inside code strips — with one exception: Contact Red may color the contact entry's text accents and nav link. A hue as a background field or headline color is a violation.

rules.name: The Entry Header Rule
rules.body: Every section opens with the same machined header row: catalog number · code strip · section title. No section may invent a different header grammar.

dos: Do keep every claim true today; the Work entry renders only when a case-study file exists, and each new case study takes the next catalog number.
Do keep the offer and email legible as plain text in the first viewport and the closing entry.
Do give every interactive element a hard inverted hover state and visible keyboard focus.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: plot static and complete, reveals settled, no rotation.
donts: Don't use glows, neon edges, scanlines, gradients, blur, or any dark-dashboard garnish — the world is matte print, not CRT.
Don't let a hue escape its code block (Contact Red's defined roles excepted).
Don't hide meaning behind code alone — every code strip sits beside plain words.
Don't carry over the ember palette or fuse-line motifs from the replaced world.
